channel.title: AI Campaign News (AICN)
channel.description: A tracker of AI use in political campaigns, elections, and advocacy.

item.title: AI Didn’t Make Me Faster. It Made Me Better.
item.description: A campaign creative professional writing in Campaigns & Elections argues that AI did not speed up their workflow but instead raised the quality of their creative output, describing a labor-intensive new process built around AI tools.

item.title: How AI deepfakes are upending political advertising
item.description: WBUR's On Point reports that AI-generated political ads flooded television and social media during the 2026 midterm cycle, with roughly half depicting real candidates' likenesses and most carrying no AI disclosure.

item.title: Political Campaigns Are Using Generative AI for Conversations with Voters
item.description: The Brennan Center for Justice documents that political campaigns in the 2026 cycle deployed generative AI chatbots to hold direct conversations with voters, raising concerns that voters may receive false information or commitments the campaign does not actually endorse.

item.title: Chatbots Became The Voter Guide
item.description: Campaign Trend reports that AI chatbots functioned as voter guides during the 2026 elections and that AI canvassers sent text messages directly to voters, while also noting a spam-trap vulnerability in Democrats' digital outreach.

item.title: Exclusive: Conservative group issues warning on AI
item.description: A post-midterms memo from the Alliance for a Better Future, a conservative AI policy group, warns Republicans that they need a major strategic recalibration on AI before the next presidential election.

item.title: Exclusive / Election 'war rooms' enter the AI age
item.description: Semafor reports that both OpenAI and Anthropic set up dedicated 'war rooms' during the 2026 midterm elections to ensure their platforms provided accurate electoral information, marking a formal operational commitment by the two leading AI labs to election integrity on their products.

item.title: Exclusive / Democrats run more anti-tech ads amid AI boom
item.description: An analysis cited by Semafor found that liberal candidates in more than 130 federal and gubernatorial races this cycle ran anti-tech or anti-data-center ads, making opposition to AI infrastructure a measurable campaign message strategy in the 2026 midterms.

item.title: ChatGPT provided Democracy Works info to voters more than 16 million times this cycle
item.description: The Hill reports that ChatGPT served election information sourced from Democracy Works to voters more than 16 million times during the 2026 election cycle, making OpenAI's chatbot a significant channel for electoral information delivery at scale.

item.title: Synthetic Voters Aren’t Voters: Where AI Belongs in Campaign Research and Where It Doesn’t
item.description: A Campaigns & Elections op-ed argues that AI synthetic respondents have a legitimate but limited role in campaign research — useful for rapid message testing and hypothesis generation, but fundamentally different from real voters and unsuitable as a direct polling substitute.

item.title: You Stopped Answering Pollsters. Campaigns Built AI Voters.
item.description: Business Model Analyst reports that AI synthetic polling vendors Aaru and Simile have each reached billion-dollar valuations as campaigns in the 2026 midterms increasingly use their platforms to replace traditional polling, with Election Day results now serving as a real-world accuracy test for the technology.

item.title: 217 Million Voters, One Chat Box: New AI Tool Opens Up the Voter File
item.description: A new AI chatbot called Voter Count allows anyone to query a database of 217 million registered voters using plain-English questions, making voter-file demographic and voting data accessible without expensive data contracts or technical skills.

item.title: AI chatbots are becoming political advisers. Their answers can mislead voters
item.description: NPR reports that AI chatbots are being used as political advisers ahead of the 2026 midterms and that their answers can mislead voters on electoral information.

item.title: UK politicians turn to AI-generated focus groups to test messages
item.description: UK politicians are testing campaign messages on AI-generated focus groups sold by vendors such as Electric Twin, which offer synthetic voter panels at a fraction of the cost of traditional focus groups.

item.title: Synthetic public opinion polling: AI personas don't always change their minds like real voters do
item.description: Research reported by Phys.org finds that AI personas used in synthetic public-opinion polling do not update their views the way real voters do when exposed to new information, raising questions about the technique's reliability for campaign research.

item.title: Field Report: How AI is Being Used in the 2026 Midterms
item.description: The Harvard Ash Center has published a field report documenting how campaigns and outside groups are deploying AI tools in the 2026 midterms, covering applications from voter contact to ad production.

item.title: Campaign texts, now powered by AI: How new tech is shaping voter outreach
item.description: CBS News reports that campaigns in the 2026 midterms are using AI-powered texting platforms to conduct voter outreach at scale, with some programs designed not just for listening but for persuasion.

item.title: AI-powered robocalls attack Talarico on data centers
item.description: CNN's KFile reports that AI-powered robocalls targeting Texas candidate Brian Talarico attacked him on the issue of data centers, a distinct deployment from the broader Republican AI ad strategy previously reported.

item.title: Websites pretending to be local news are boosting Democratic candidates
item.description: NPR reports that websites impersonating local news outlets are using ChatGPT to generate content boosting Democratic candidates in the 2026 midterms.

item.title: Why AI Chatbots Love Ballotpedia, and What Candidates Should Do About It
item.description: Ballotpedia's Leslie Graves explains why major AI chatbots frequently cite Ballotpedia as a primary source for candidate information, and outlines concrete steps campaigns can take to ensure their candidates' Ballotpedia profiles are accurate and optimized to influence AI-generated answers.

item.title: AI Is Reshaping Political Ads — and You Might Not Even Know It
item.description: A Katie Couric Media overview reports that AI-generated political ads are proliferating in the 2026 midterms, describing them as cheaper and harder for voters to detect than traditionally produced spots.

item.title: Meet Haystack: Social Listening Built for Democrats
item.description: Higher Ground Labs has announced Haystack, an AI-native social listening platform designed for Democratic communicators to monitor what voters are seeing and saying on social media.

item.title: Democrats are betting GOP's AI ads on Talarico and others will backfire
item.description: The Washington Post reports that Democratic campaigns are deliberately avoiding AI-generated video ads, betting that Republican use of such ads — including against candidates like Brian Talarico in Texas — will generate a backlash among voters skeptical of AI content.

item.title: Scoop: Washington Democrats allege AI misuse in GOP-backed mailer
item.description: Washington state Democrats allege that a GOP-backed mailer supporting candidate Michael Shepard misused AI, potentially in violation of Washington election law, according to Axios Seattle.

item.title: Congressman faces ethics complaint over AI generated graphic of opponent
item.description: A U.S. congressman is facing an ethics complaint after circulating an AI-generated graphic depicting an opponent, according to a local news report.

item.title: AI is reshaping high-stakes elections around the world
item.description: Semafor reports that partisan actors in Brazil, Israel, and the U.S. are gaming AI platforms to surface misleading information ahead of high-stakes elections, describing a cross-border pattern of AI-answer manipulation tied to active campaigns.

item.title: Exclusive: Democratic AI PAC takes its fight to Senate Republicans
item.description: Tomorrow Together, a Democratic PAC advocating for AI regulation, is spending $2.5 million on ads targeting Republican Senators Jon Husted in Ohio and Roger Marshall in Kansas, expanding its campaign beyond House races into competitive Senate contests.

item.title: UK Politicians Are Testing Their Messages on AI-Generated Focus Groups
item.description: UK politicians are using AI-generated focus groups — synthetic respondents — to pre-test campaign messaging before deploying it to real audiences, according to Bloomberg reporting.

item.title: The next election influence campaign will target your AI chatbot
item.description: Israeli threat intelligence firm VisionHeight has identified a coordinated network of at least 460 pages across 37 websites in 14 states — including Arizona, Georgia, Michigan, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin — publishing AI-optimized content designed to steer chatbot responses toward specific candidates in House races, Secretary of State contests, and local offices. The sites, with names like "Wolverine State Report" and "Peach State Bulletin," were configured to allow major AI crawlers to scrape them, and at least one — Tarheel State Report — was cited as a primary source by Perplexity; VisionHeight does not attribute the operation to a specific actor.

item.title: AI is changing what political campaigns say, and who gets to hear it
item.description: An AP report, syndicated from Minneapolis, examines how political campaigns are using AI to tailor messaging at the individual voter level — analyzing consumer data such as vehicle ownership, shopping habits, and homeownership to personalize outreach at scale in ways previously unavailable to most campaigns.

item.title: Voters Are Already Getting AI Answers About Your Campaign. They Just Don't Know It.
item.description: A new AAPC Foundation national survey of likely voters, discussed by Tarrance Group pollster B.J. Martino, finds that voters are already encountering AI-generated answers about campaigns through ambient AI tool use — often without knowing it — and that significant voter distrust and hard limits around campaign AI use are emerging from the data.
